articleTitle: Distributed Piecewise Droop Control of DC Microgrid with Improved Load Sharing and Voltage Compensation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Droop control is an essential part of primary control in hierarchical control paradigm of DC microgrid. However, the problem with basic droop control using constant virtual resistance is that higher current sharing accuracy was achieved at the cost of higher bus voltage deviation, and thus which will degrade power quality and system efficiency of DC microgrid. In this paper, a family of distributed piecewise droop control strategies (DPDC) are derived to overcome the shortcomings of basic droop control in primary control level where the droop curves are configured flexibly according to partitioned load regions, and as a result, both current sharing and voltage compensation will be improved simultaneously. The superior performance of the DPDC strategies are verified by hardware testing results.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Isolated Ripple Cancel Dual Active Bridge DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The bidirectional isolated dual active bridge DC-DC converter has been widely used for high power applications. The converter features a simple configuration, high efficiency, compact size, and flexible design. However, DC-link capacitors suffer from high current ripple that limits the lifetime of aluminum electrolytic capacitors. In addition, the power rating of DC-DC applications is growing more and more nowadays. One example, is ultra-fast charging stations for future electric vehicles. Accordingly, the design of DC-link capacitors faces high current ripple issue, that is to say, the challenge of converter reliability and volume selection. To solve this problem, a ripple cancel type dual active bridge converter is proposed in this paper. By adding few small size and capacitance film or ceramic capacitors, the current ripple of the DC-link capacitor could be significantly reduced. Input/output voltage ripple could be reduced as well. In addition, the voltage stress of the main switches could be clamped without additional snubber capacitors. Furthermore, the circuit design is similar to the conventional DAB converter. A 1kW prototype was implemented with a 400 V input/output voltage and a 100 kHz switching frequency to demonstrate its feasibility. The RMS current of the DC-link capacitor was reduced to 125mA in the experiment.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a DC Microgrid with Central Operation Strategies on an Island
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper introduces and discusses a DC microgrid constructed on an island. KEPCO constructed a DC microgrid system on an island called Seogeochado (West Geocha Island) through the `DC Island' project. With regard to the DC Island project, which operates a DC system from generation source to customer, this paper examines the development of LVDC equipment and the implementation of an LVDC microgrid system based on calculations of the optimal renewable energy capacity performed by HOMER, an economic feasibility analysis tool. Also, this paper suggests a centralized operation method for the DC system that optimizes the operation of a DC microgrid on an island and discusses its demonstration.

articleTitle: Novel Fault Tolerant DC-DC Converter Architecture for LED Lighting Systems Operating in DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The ever-increasing evidences showing the benefits related to the transition to a more sustainable framework of energy distribution at buildings, based on DC microgrids, calls for the development of suitable technologies. Residential lighting systems based on LED technologies gain further significance as these technologies become mature. Unfortunately, power electronic technologies used to drive LED lighting systems are unable to correspond with the longevity levels of LED devices. Particularly, active semiconductors pose one of the major hurdles to the full exploitation of the LED lifetime. Accordingly, the development of reliable LED driving systems, capable of fully exploiting the lifetime of LEDs, becomes critical. Keeping in mind that adoption of DC microgrids at homes and offices is a scenario that is rapidly taking shape, it is important to develop power conversion solutions for such end. This paper proposes a fault tolerant LED driving system, based on a DC-DC converter, suitable for residential DC microgrids.

articleTitle: Autonomous DC Microgrid Consisting of Triple Active Bridge Converters
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: We propose an autonomous DC microgrid consisting of triple active bridge (TAB) converters. In microgrids, various renewable energies, batteries, and local consumer appliances could be integrated by using TAB converters with different operating DC voltages such as 400-V DC bus voltages, 110-V battery systems, and 48-V ICT equipment. We constructed a prototype TAB converter rated at 10 kW and developed a decoupling power flow control system with a voltage difference between each port of the TAB converter. The prototype rated at 400 V/400 V/48 V was implemented to demonstrate the feasibility of the control system. In addition, a linearized model of mutually connected TAB converters was investigated. An experiment using prototype TAB converters was conducted to validate the control system based on the model. When the power flow pattern among the ports of the converters changed in step, the power value of each port converged to the desired power value. Therefore, we conclude that TAB converters can be stably operated by using the developed control system even when TAB converters are connected in series.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Hybrid DC Circuit Breaker based on Counter-Current Injection Method for Low-Voltage DC Grids
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Isolating the faults in low-voltage DC grids remains a major technical obstacle in designing the protection system for LVDC grids [1]. Conventional mechanical circuit breakers need to be connected in series to make them compatible for DC grids and they are still not fast enough to disconnect the DC faults with fast rising DC short-circuit currents. In this paper, performance of a hybrid DC circuit breaker topology using a counter-current injection method for producing current-zero switching [2] is analyzed. The topology allows use of a mechanical circuit breaker assisted with power electronic based auxiliary circuit for the switching of DC currents at minimal arcing. A thyristor is used instead of mechanical circuit breaker to enforce switching at current-zero crossing. The circuit breaker topology is simulated in Matlab/Simulink and implemented in hardware for 380Vdc networks. The study analyzes the effect of different circuit elements on the maximum interruption capability and turn-off time of the circuit breaker.

articleTitle: A Multivariable Hysteresis-Based DC Bus Signaling Control for DC Microgrid With Enhanced Reliability
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Using DC bus signaling to realize autonomous coordinated operation of DC microgrid is a well-known strategy for power management without extra communication. While this powerful method achieves economic, plug-and-play, and reliable operation of DC microgrid, the high dependency of operating modes on bus voltage still creates potential threat to reliable operation of the system, especially if there is disturbance or interference on the bus voltage. A multivariable hysteresis-based DC bus signaling control (MVH-DBS) is proposed in this paper. By introducing another variable besides DC bus voltage to formulate the MVH-DBS strategy, operation modes transitions of each unit in the DC microgrid are coordinated by two sensed variables instead of only bus voltage in existing methods. As a result, reliability of autonomously coordinated operation of DC microgrid can be significantly improved. Simulation results validate the proposed MVH-DBS strategy.

articleTitle: DC Voltage Stabilization in DC/AC Hybrid Microgrid by Cooperative Control of Multiple Energy Storages
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper presents experimental study results compared with simulation study results for the voltage stabilization of a hybrid microgrid system, which may be possibly deteriorated by both integration of RES (Renewable Energy Sources) power generation and load variation. The experimental studies have been carried out by use of a small-scale prototype microgrid system that has been developed by Tohoku Gakuin University, Japan for the research and development of microgrid related technologies. In the proposed microgrid system, both DC and AC power can be directly supplied to the corresponding type of loads, and the degraded DC voltage due to RES and load power fluctuation is stabilized by cooperative control of two different types of energy storage, which are EDLC (Electrical Double Layer Capacitor) and secondary battery, respectively. In simulation studies, the microgrid model with the similar system configuration of experimental studies has been worked out, and simulations have been conducted for identifying the voltage stabilizing effect for the proposed microgrid system. This paper gives the results obtained from both experimental and simulation studies, and these results illustrate the DC voltage can be effectively stabilized by the cooperative control of energy storages.

articleTitle: State of Charge Based Characteristic Diagram Control for Energy Storage Systems within Industrial DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In this paper, a state of charge (SoC) based characteristic diagram control concept for energy storage systems (ESS) within an industrial direct current (DC) microgrid is proposed. The inputs are the SoC of the ESS and the terminal voltage of the DC microgrid. The output is the charge and discharge current for the converter, which connects the ESS with the DC microgrid. An appropriate design concept for the characteristic diagram is then investigated to achieve a flexible control reacting on changing conditions within the DC microgrid. These could be a temporary overload, due to a changing number of grid participants or an additional feed-in through a photovoltaic (PV) system. The characteristic diagram design concept is even applicable without a deep knowledge of the load profile of the DC microgrid. The concept was analyzed and evaluated based on simulations with load profiles from robot cells. The results show that the SoC depends on the current load of the DC microgrid. If the load returns to average, the SoC of the ESS inclines back to the nominal SoC, which is pre-defined by the grid operator. Furthermore, in case of an appropriate design of the characteristic diagram, it can protect the ESS against overcharging or deep discharging.

articleTitle: Polar Coordinate Decoupling Power Flow Control for Triple Active Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: A triple active bridge converter can play a role of energy management in dc grids and help to construct them including distributed power systems and loads. However, the control system of a triple active bridge converter is a 2-input 2-output system. Therefore, a decoupling control is necessary. In a conventional control method, the decoupling matrix is designed as an inverse of the small signal transfer function matrix. However, the transfer function matrix is developed by approximation, causing the errors in the decoupling matrix. There has a little interference by using this conventional decoupling control method. This paper proposes a novel decoupling power flow control method for triple active bridge converters. The polar coordinate directly determines the phase shifts between the ports by utilizing the amplitude and the phase angle represented by the sum and the difference of transmission powers. This method is expected to get faster responses by using feedforward control and to achieve precise decoupling. The experimental results validate these expectations.

articleTitle: Simulation Research on the Operation Characteristics of a DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: DC microgrid power supply can not only solve the problem of excessive line loss of the large power grid effectively, but also increase the reliability of power supply. It is economic and environmental, and it also helps to improve energy utilization efficiency. Different microgrid topologies of the DC microgrid system are summarized and compared and a monopole bus microgrid is simulated. The operation characteristics of the system with PV array and battery are analyzed which can provide guidelines for the design of a DC microgrid system.

articleTitle: Cooperative Decentralized Tertiary Based Control of DC Microgrid with Renewable Distributed Generation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper introduces a cooperative decentralized control strategy to control power management in a DC microgrid integrated with multiple energy Renewable energy sources (RES) mainly of Photovoltaic (PV), and conventional distributed generations (DGs). Control strategy is based on a hierarchical structure of primary, secondary and tertiary controllers. DC bus voltage signal is used to enable power sharing among different power sources and for seamless transition between modes of operation. Primary control is mainly based on an adaptive droop mechanism [1], [2] to regulate voltage output of each converter and balance generation amongst sources. Secondary controller is applied to measure voltage across the micro grid and update voltage setpoint for primary controllers. Consequently, Tertiary controller is a higher-level controller, that is responsible for the economic dispatch of all power sources in the whole dc microgrid cluster. A cooperative control strategy is applied to implement the primary, secondary and tertiary controllers. Recent research papers had implemented tertiary controller in a single mode dc microgrids to control voltage setpoints and perform economic dispatch of power generation. Moreover, this paper discusses stability issues introduced by constant power loads. Constant power loads (CPL) are one of the main factors causing destabilization in dc microgrids by which the main bus voltage shows significant oscillations and may collapse. Distributed generations are connected to the microgrid thorough Line Regulating Converters (LRC). However, novelty of this paper is in implementing cooperative decentralized voltage and current control, based on dead zone and power generation capacity, to mitigate voltage oscillations in dc microgrids and to reduce the entire generation cost by controlling voltage output of every single power converter. Ultimately, the effectiveness of the proposed technique is verified using MATLAB/SIMULINK 2016b based on a composite dc microgrid test system.

articleTitle: Supercapacitor Assisted LED lighting (SCALED) for DC-micro grids
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: High conversion efficiency in converters is the key to reduce power consumption in electronics. System modules in whitegoods, lighting and portables are internally DC-powered, and this motivates DC microgrid powering. When multiple conversion stages are cascaded, end-to-end efficiency (ETEE) is given by the product of efficiency ratios. If DC directly powers a system, elimination of AC-DC conversion means ETEE will be higher. Commercially available 12 V LED luminaires can be used with solar and other renewable energy sources with high efficiency and no electricity bills. However, the fluctuating nature of renewable sources such as solar requires short and long-term energy storage for reliable DC powering. Given the long life cycles of supercapacitors (SC), compared to electrochemical batteries, despite their lower energy density, SCs can be used to buffer short-term power fluctuations. Supercapacitor charging is challenging because unlike batteries, SCs do not act as resistive loads. This is because when a capacitor is fed with a charge of Q coulombs, it only stores 0.5 QV while an equal amount of energy is lost in parasitic circuit resistances. SCALED (Supercapacitor Assisted LED) is a new approach where a significant part of this loss is diverted to LED lamps in the SC charging path, thereby increasing the ETEE of a 12 V DC-fed LED-powering system from 50% to ~90%. This paper presents details of this SCALED conversion system, under development for Ports of Auckland seaport lighting systems, including theory and experimental efficiency measurements.

articleTitle: Lifetime Calculation for Capacitors in Industrial Micro DC grids
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This article deals with the determination of the lifetime of electrolytic capacitors operating in industrial DC micro grids, which are characterized by a particular large number of electrical drives. In addition to the advantages of such a DC grid, a test setup is proposed as a solution that allows an easy device testing. The paper shows with the help of simulations and practical measurements that if every device passes this test, it can be ensured that no capacitor in the DC grid is overloaded at all.

articleTitle: Simplification of Electric Substation System by Utilizing Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: An innovative application of an energy storage system as replacement of traction substation has been proposed and tested to simplify power supply system configuration. The tests were carried out at Ohnuki Susbstation on the Uchibo Line of East Japan Railway Company in 2017 and 2018. This paper presents an overview of our proposal and some key figures of the test to explain the feasibility of the system.

articleTitle: Decentralized Control-Scheme for DC-Interconnected Solar Home Systems for Rural Electrification
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Solar Home Systems (SHS) have proven to be an effective means to tackle the global energy poverty that still affects around 1 billion people. However, present-day SHS (which are standalone systems with usually a purely dc architecture) have a limited power rating (usually up to 100 Wp). To enable higher power levels of electricity access in an economically viable way, energy sharing between these individual SHS through interconnectivity is a logical progression. The interconnectivity has to be implemented at a higher voltage level in order to reduce the conduction losses and cable costs. Existing control schemes do not take into account the multi-voltage dc microgrids. In this paper, the state of charge (SOC) balancing in such an interconnected SHS-based dc microgrid is addressed. In particular, the adaptive droop-based SOC control is extended for multiple voltage levels in a dc microgrid without any means of active communication. This is achieved through the creation of a voltage dead-band, SOC-based droop resistances, and the use of voltage ratios in dc-dc converters.

articleTitle: Parametric Analysis of Centralized DC Microgrids for Rural Electrification
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Many solar photovoltaic (PV) based DC microgrids have been deployed in the recent past for supplying electricity facilities to the rural areas in developing regions. In this work, we assess various parameters that may impact the operational efficiencies of centralized DC microgrids. Primarily, we evaluate distribution losses in a typical system with varying critical system parameters such as a) distribution voltage b) distribution conductor size c) amount of load to be delivered at each connected rural house and d) system size (number of subscribing houses). The losses are evaluated using Newton-Raphson method modified for DC power flow and a general framework is given for loss evaluation in custom distribution architectures. Quantified system performance for a typical microgrid system from the perspective of distribution losses and maximal voltage dips will be highly useful for future solar PV-based microgrid installations.

articleTitle: Hybrid AC/DC Microgrid for Residential Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In this paper, we present the architecture and feasibility analysis of a hybrid AC/DC microgrid for residential applications. Although AC is ruling the building distribution architecture for years, however now DC is also appearing as a strong contestant due to a) large penetration of solar PV in residential power networks, b) decreasing prices of battery storage and c) market availability of highly efficient DC loads. Adding an extra DC distribution layer in conjunction with the existing AC distribution can reduce overall losses in the path of power flow from the source end to the load end. Therefore, we propose a hybrid AC/DC microgrid capable of driving AC loads through AC power and DC loads through DC power, thereby minimizing AC/DC interconversion losses. The interlinking AC/DC converter in the proposed architecture allows bi-directional power transformation between AC and DC sub-grids, thereby, enables efficient resource utilization. The framework for the analysis of distribution and power electronic interconversion losses is presented. For a typical urban household load variations, a fair comparison among AC-only, DC-only, and hybrid AC/DC microgrid suggests that hybrid AC/DC microgrid can significantly enhance the efficiency of residential power systems.

articleTitle: Grid Flexibility Dispatch by Integrated Control of Distributed Energy Resources
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The authors proposed grid flexibility dispatch by controlling distributed energy resources (DER) of prosumers to respond to high penetration of variable renewable energy sources. DER are interconnected via DC link and can be controlled flexibly by an energy management system (EMS), which is installed to a prosumer. The prosumers buy/sell electricity and supply flexibility to markets via an aggregator. An operational simulation was performed to evaluate possibility of flexibility dispatch by DER responding to incentives.

articleTitle: PV-grid performance under dynamic weather conditions
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper presents results from research in the stability of DC/AC power generated by PV (photo voltaic) systems. It is well known that the generated power can change abruptly due to especially moving clouds, causing potential instability of the DC/AC power grid. The transient behavior of moving clouds is analyzed in detail via long term (several years) high speed recording of panel/inverter performance, as well as high speed recording of IV-curves of selected panels performed under Scandinavian as well as Italian weather conditions. The performance of string inverters and central inverters are analyzed and compared. The result of > 10 mill. recordings are presented by graphical and statistical means and show an extremely low occurrence of Standard Test Condition (STC) conditions).

articleTitle: Power Packet Dispatching System and Router for Bi-directional Dispatching
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Power packet dispatching system is proposed as one of the advanced dc power distribution systems. In order to manage the flow of power packet in the distribution system according to the tag information attached to the power packet, the router, which dispatches the packets, a key element of the system. In this paper, a router is invented to dispatch the packets by-directionally. The laboratory prototype router applies SiC MOSFET for the power switches. The bi-directional router enables us to select the setting points to connect power sources and loads in the system more flexibly.

articleTitle: AC vs. DC Boost Converters: A Detailed Conduction Loss Comparison
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Studies have shown the efficiency benefits of DC distribution systems are largely due to the superior performance of DC/DC converters. Nonetheless, these studies are often based on product data that differs widely in manufacturer and operating voltage. This work develops a rigorous loss model to theoretically compare the efficiency of a DC/DC and an AC/DC PFC boost converter. It ensures each converter has the same components and equivalent operating voltages. The results show AC boost converters below 500 W to have 2.9 to 4.2 times the loss of DC.

articleTitle: DC Microgrid Experimental System at KIT Hakusan-roku Campus for Regional Areas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: We describe our DC Microgrid experimental system at Kanazawa Institute of Technology (KIT) Hakusan-roku campus located at regional area of Hakusan city in Japan. Our experimental system is at the first stage of our roadmap in which our final goal is to construct a DC Microgrid network system in all of our campus. This system consists of DC bus, PV, battery, EV and a biomass system which is directly connected to DC bus. We describe backgrounds the reason why we choose DC system for our Microgrid. Then, we show the overview of system configuration and the concept of system control method that is composed by three-layer hybrid strategy using heat and electricity. The DC system which is the electrical part of our Microgrid is controlled by distributed way using equal incremental charge loading method.

articleTitle: DC Bus System for Servo Drives and its Stability Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: A servo drive has been used widely in the industrial market. Recently, utilizing the regenerative energy of the motor has become important in the drive for energy efficiency. Also, the problems of EMI noise and complexity of wiring from a 3-phase PWM inverter became obvious in the factory application as well. A DC bus system should be a solution because it can handle a battery for the regenerative energy easily, and an integrating servo drive with motor does not diffuse noise. Further, it can save wiring dramatically. However, the system has a risk of instability between the DC bus line and the servo drives. In this paper, an impedance-based stability analysis method is introduced for the DC bus system of the servo drive. The system instability was demonstrated experimentally, and the theoretical and measured results are matching within 10% accuracy.

articleTitle: A 13.2kV / 150kVA Solid State Transformer for a Bipolar LVDC Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In this paper, in order to supply a bipolar ± 750 V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DC</sub> for LVDC distribution system, a 13.2kV<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">AC</sub> / 150kVA solid state transformer (SST) was proposed. This prototype SST was installed in Go-Chang which is DC distribution test site in Korea. The design and performance of the proposed SST are verified by experimental results using a 150kVA prototype.

articleTitle: Medium voltage cable designs for 100km DC superconducting power transmission line using experimental data of Ishikari Project
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Main two merits of the DC superconducting power transmission line are low loss and zero resistance of the cable. Since it is a small system, its system cost will be lower than the copper cable system finally. The loss of the DC superconducting power transmission line depends on the heat leak from the cryogenic pipe and the COP of the refrigerator, therefore the main subject is to minimize the electric power consumption of cryogenic refrigerator system, and we should realize low heat leak from the cryogenic pipe, and high COP of the refrigerator is required. At the same time, low circulation power of liquid nitrogen is necessary. The heat leak of cryogenic pipe lower than 1 Watt/meter was realized in Ishikari project in 2016 in very low pressure drop of the cryogen circulation. We also should pay attention on the temperature rise of the cable for a longer transmission. The temperature rise is only ~0.03 K/km in Ishikari project because of the radiation shield structure. Therefore, we could construct 100km transmission line basically, and the cooling stations are located at both ends. We investigate several parameters of the cable designs, and its voltage will be 25kV, and the current is available up to 10kA. Because of this, we can connect the power stations to the distribution substations directly, and we can omit high voltage substations. Medium voltage power converter was proposed and is developed for renewable energy system. Finally, we can realize the main two merits of DC superconducting power transmission line.

Author Keywords: medium voltage and large current system

articleTitle: Supercapacitor Assisted Data Center Power Architecture for 380 V DC-microgrid
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Powering a data center is a challenge due to high demand for cloud market and the increasing power density of servers. All major cloud service providers are moving towards energy-wise self-sustained datacenters powered by renewable energy sources. However, when a DC-microgrid solely depends on these sources, power output fluctuations need to be tackled by suitable energy storage devices. The supercapacitor assisted DC-DC converter design presented here is aimed at higher power density server racks supplied by DC-microgrid. In this new power converter topology, a supercapacitor (SC) bank is introduced series to the isolation transformer to temporarily storing energy. The output stage is based on the supercapacitor assisted low dropout regulator (SCALDO) technique to enhance the power quality and efficiency. This new converter is high power, maintenance free alternative to existing battery-based UPS systems.

articleTitle: Enhanced Protection Selectivity in LVDC networks using a Superconducting Resistance
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Low voltage direct current (LVDC) distribution systems have recently been considered as an alternative approach to facilitate the integration of distributed energy resources (DERs). However, DC protection is one of the key challenges facing the wider uptake of LVDC technologies. This is due the sensitivity of DC systems to rapid depression of DC voltages caused by short circuit faults, making DC fault location and protection selectivity very challenging. Superconducting materials are commonly used as part of a fault current limiter in AC and DC systems predominantly as a passive device, that can provide variable impedance during DC fault conditions whilst not impacting on the dynamic response of the grid during normal operation. Therefore, this paper presents a novel utilization of a superconducting resistance primarily as an indicator of fault location. The objective is to improve the selectivity of LVDC protection schemes where discerning between fault locations, particularly in electronic-based substations, is problematic.

articleTitle: A study on estimation of arc parameters for low voltage DC arc breaking process
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: We aim at constructing a DC arc black-box model. As a first step, in this paper, DC breaking experiments were carried out. The arc-quenching device is connected in series with resistance R, inductor L, switch S, and DC source of E=120 V. The interruption tests were conducted for three cases of DC current, IDC of 5 A, 15 A, and 20 A, under the circuit conditions without L and with L=3.3 mH and 6.6 mH. Arc parameter sets were estimated by using the Mayr's equation. In Mayr's equation. θ [s] and N0 [W/mm] are called the arc time constant and arc power loss, respectively. Assuming that the product of θ and N0, Q=θN0 [J/mm], was constant, the time variations in θ and N0 for various magnitude of Q were estimated from the measured arc voltage and current waveforms by iterative calculation so that the resistance of the arc column per unit length obtained from the Mayr equation agreed with the measured one. The dependence of the arc parameter on the corresponding instantaneous current was investigated under the condition in which the inter-electrode distance is more than 5 mm, because the arc column was considered to be unstable in the inter-electrode distance less than 5 mm. As a result, it was found out that the arc parameters derived under different experimental conditions might be expressed with one function of the transient arc current.

articleTitle: Smoothing Effect and Energy Capacity in Photovoltaic Power Smoothing Control Using Spline Function
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In a photovoltaic generation system, the output power fluctuates with the weather. Hence, the power quality may deteriorate when a large number of photovoltaic generation systems are connected to the power grid. Therefore, power smoothing control methods in the photovoltaic system with an energy storage system have been proposed. This paper evaluates the relationship between the power smoothing effect and the rated capacity of the energy storage system for the power smoothing control method using the spline function which is proposed by the same authors earlier. Validation uses data of a 153-day period measured in a photovoltaic power generation system with the rated power of 1.75 MW. The smoothing effect was 51.8% using the proposed method when the lower frequency for the target frequency band of the short-term fluctuation components of the power flowing to the power grid was 1/1,200 Hz, while the rated capacity of the energy storage system was 106 kWh without energy control. Although the smoothing effect decreased, the rated capacity of the storage system could be greatly reduced by energy control.

articleTitle: MVDC ring-cable approach for new DC distribution and restructured AC grids
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid distribution grid concept, based on a MVDC (Medium Voltage DC)-ring-cable grid approach, which could substitute AC distribution transformers, enable new DC- and restructuring existing AC-grids. This paper is focused on an MVDC-ring-cable approach, integrated MVDC/LVDC-converter stages as well as DC loads, resting upon an overall concept, including grid planning and operation issues like in [1]-[8].

articleTitle: Development of a High-Speed Circuit Breaker for DC Railway Substations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Mitsubishi Electric has developed a DCCB for railway substations which has the world's fastest interruption speed, which named “type-JH High-Speed Circuit Breaker (HSCB)”. Some techniques used in the type-JH HSCB are reviewed. Based on our investigation at Feb. 2018.

articleTitle: Power electronics for a LVDC-microgrid with local PV production and electrolytic converter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The 700 V DC-microgrid installed at HES-SO Valais-Wallis integrating PV-production, battery storage and consumption, has been upgraded in terms of installed PV-power, stronger load variations, and an improved regulation scheme for the energy consumption over day-night cycle. The installed PV-power was raised from 10 kW<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> to 15 kW<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>. Whereas previously all PV-modules were injecting via individual DC/DC converters, this time a serial DC/DC converter has been developed. This allows the installation of serial PV-strings of standard dimension generally used in DC/AC based PV-plants. The grid management system now comprises a battery system of about 75 kWh nominal storage capacity that has been operated for solar peak shaving. It thus allows transferring the power surplus for reducing the exchange between the semi-autonomous DC microgrid and the AC mains. In addition, an electrolysis system is being tested to use and store surplus power. In terms of consumers, a 5kVA heat pump and a 22kVA electric car charging point have been added to the grid.

articleTitle: A soft-starting method for Dual Active Bridge Converters
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper deal with current stress during the starting time of Dual-Active-Bridge DC/DC converters. The cold-starting method and the popular soft-starting technique using Dual-Phase-Shifts (DPS) are firstly analyzed. Accordingly, mathematics equations to identify the current stress are derived. Based on that a new method is proposed that preserves the minimum current stress of the former method, whereas reduces the starting time. Experimental results confirm that current stress is reduced 40% compared to that of cold-starting method; and the starting time is shorten by 12.5% compared to that obtained by DPS method with the same current stress.

articleTitle: Stability Control Strategy for DC Micro-grid Considering Constant Power Load
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The electric load integrated in DC micro-grid is typically with the property of constant power which demonstrates negative resistor characteristics and can be a challenge for DC micro-grid stability control. Based on a large capacity DC micro-grid with variety of sources and loads and converters, the presented paper established an equivalent circuit model of the DC micro-grid system with droop control and discussed the stability issues of the system. Considering the nonlinearity of the system, this paper firstly determined the stability of the system equilibrium points. Secondly, the influence of constant power load and system parameters on the stability of the system was analyzed, and the load carrying capacity of the system under different system parameters was quantified and verified by simulation. Finally, according to the results of the stabilization mechanism analysis, the selection of control system parameters in the planning and design is discussed, and the stability control strategy of DC micro-grid was proposed from the system level combining with the hierarchical control of micro-grid, and the simulation and experimental verification were carried out.

articleTitle: Common Mode Conductive Noise Cancellation for Multiphase Converter Using Auxiliary Winding
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: A High power density DC/DC converter is often achieved by a combination of multiphase interleaved circuit topology and fast switching devices such as SiC MOSFETs or GaN FETs. On the other hand, the large dv/dt of such devices results in a large amplitude of common mode (CM) conductive noise. Therefore, CM noise attenuation is essential to take full advantage of the multiphase converter in practical application. However, no research on noise reduction methods uniquely for multiphase DC/DC converters, with loosely coupled inductor, has been conducted. Thus, in this paper, CM noise attenuation methods suitable for a multiphase converter is presented and investigated. Consequently, the result verifies that the proposed methods greatly decrease CM noise and the proposed methods encourage development in high power density power electronics.

articleTitle: Planar transformer design of LLC DC-DC converters with electromagnetics simulation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: A proper magnetic component design is required for the realization of high performance power supply unit design. However there are many tradeoffs between design parameters, such as frequency, AC resistance, leakage inductance, component size, parasitic capacitance and cost demand. To meet these requirements, effective usage of the electromagnetic simulation is gathering attention. Furthermore, multi-physics simulation that combines several physical simulation such as electromagnetics, fluid, thermal conductivity and mechanical stress enables us to make virtual prototypes of the real products. In this paper, design parameters of planar transformers for various LLC DC-DC converters are investigated with iterative EM simulation and optimization of winding structures are demonstrated. Also as an evaluation example of multi-domain simulation, electromagnetics and circuit co-simulation is performed. Transformers and resonance inductors of LLC power supply circuit are 3D-geometrically modeled and AC characteristics of these inductors are simulated with full-wave electromagnetic simulation software. Simulated characteristics are extracted and imported to the circuit simulation software and the circuit simulation with detailed magnetic component model is realized. The evaluation target is 240 W LLC DC-DC converter. Experimental results show that measured and simulated waveforms and conversion efficiency have good correlation. Therefore, the effectiveness of electromagnetics and circuit co-simulation for the precise behavior prediction of the LLC converter circuit is confirmed.

articleTitle: Voltage Control of High-voltage Distribution System Using Distributed Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel method to reduce the opportunity loss of power generation and maintain the system voltage within the specified range when photovoltaic generation systems are intensively connected to the high-voltage distribution system. The proposed method suppresses the voltage rise caused by surplus power of photovoltaic generation systems by charging electric vehicles. Furthermore, when the system voltage cannot be suppressed by only electric vehicles, power conditioning systems of photovoltaic systems are used cooperatively. The power conditioning system performs active power control. In addition, the proposed method suppresses the voltage drop by discharging electric vehicles. The usefulness of the proposed method is verified by computer simulation. As a result, the opportunity loss of power generation in the photovoltaic generation system was reduced from 18.5% to 5.25% of the total electric energy of all nodes with charging and discharging control of electric vehicles. The power generated by the photovoltaic generation system can be effectively utilized and the voltage in the high-voltage distribution system is maintained within the specified range.

articleTitle: Cooperative Control of Multi-Input Modular DC/DC Converter for Electric Off-Highway Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper proposes a cooperative control used in a power conversion system consists of several energy sources and modular DC/DC converters. The proposed cooperative control method has attractive features of realizing constant dynamic characteristics even when each input voltage fluctuates or in case of the output power of each input voltage source is limited. The proposed cooperative control method has dual control loops with current control as an inner loop and voltage control as the outer loop. In addition, feed-forward control of the input voltage and the compensators for each control loop are implemented to suppress the influence of input voltage fluctuation or power capacity limit on dynamic characteristics. The effectiveness of the proposed control is validated by simulation test.

articleTitle: A New Protection Scheme Using an AC/DC Converter for a LVDC Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: As the number of direct current (DC) customers is currently expanding, and distribution lines are changing from alternative current (AC) to DC accordingly, DC distribution lines with a radial structure are also becoming longer. This paper includes an analysis of the characteristics of fault currents in LVDC systems, and proposes a protective coordination method, utilizing AC/DC converters and protection equipment when a fault occurs in direct current lines with radial structure, that has been effectively demonstrated in field verification tests.

articleTitle: Improving Efficiency, Reliability and Life-time Cost of Data Centers Using DC Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: With the expansion of today's digital era, the use of electronic equipment is increasing exponentially at home, office, and plants. The common denominator of these electronic equipment is that they all use Direct current (DC) power internally by converting Alternating Current (AC) power to DC power using local converters. All these converters produce losses, heat, and are prone to failures which in turn impact the equipment efficiency, life span, and reliability. In addition, these converters increase the cost of equipment they are powering and their required footprint. The issue of reliability and cost reduction is more stressing for data centers where servers, Uninterruptable Power Supply (UPS) systems, and IT equipment constituting the majority of the load can be powered directly through a DC grid. This paper presents a case study that compares AC and DC technologies for powering a typical data center and outlines the main advantages and limitations of each technology. This study will present a comparative analysis of a DC power system against a typical AC distribution for critical datacenter loads. It also presents a real case study of existing AC powered data center and compare the benefits of powering the center via DC instead of AC. Analytical reliability, safety and efficiency models are developed, and quantitative results are obtained based on a set of real data. The study indicates that the DC system would be more reliable, efficient and will achieve less Capex and Opex values than the AC.

Author Keywords: Efficiency and Total Cost of Ownership

articleTitle: The Efficiency Estimation Method for Harvesting Energy Charged into Capacitor
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to give the estimation diagram of the direct charging efficiency by the energy harvesting. The energy generated by energy harvester is very small. In many cases we can't use DC/DC converter because the generated power is very small comparing to the power of the device driving or the converting efficiency is very small at those region. In such case, we sometimes use the method of the direct charging into the capacitor. But it is so hard to estimate the energy charging efficiency intuitively. The average efficiency is fundamentally related to the open voltage and the short current of the energy harvester and depends on the initial voltage and charged up voltage of the capacitor. We have derived the energy charging efficiency on the capacitor by using only four parameters. By using those relationships I have given the simple diagram for estimation of the charging efficiency. It is remarkable that the charging duration and the charging capacitance are not concerned with that result. Then we can use any capacitor for the efficiency estimation. Finally I have examined this diagram validity by the charging measurement of energy harvester.

articleTitle: Impedance Measurement Method for Solar Cell Evaluation using a Power Converter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This study aims to present an impedance measurement method using a power converter to evaluate degradation of solar panels. The ac impedance method is used to evaluate electrochemical devices, such as fuel cells and batteries. Herein, we conducted experiments to measure the impedance frequency characteristics of photovoltaic panels under normal and partially shaded conditions. Results show that the impedance under a partially shaded condition is higher than that under a normal condition.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Converter with Balancing Capacitor using Multi-stage FET Driving Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper proposes a bidirectional converter with balancing capacitor using multi-stage FET driving technique. The proposed converter is constructed by implementing series-connected low voltage Si-FETs in multi-stages. The balancing capacitor can average the applied voltage on FETs in the transient state of the switching operation and tackle the voltage unbalance between the series-connected FETs. The proposed driving circuit is using multi-stage FET driving technique and can drive all the series-connected FETs using only one power supply. The effect of the balancing capacitor and the proposed driving technique are clarified and presented using the circuit simulator and the converter equivalent circuit. The proposed topology improves the converter power conversion efficiency. The experimental results show that the proposed driving technique allows the bidirectional converter to achieve a maximum power conversion efficiency of 99.2%.

articleTitle: A Study on Allocation Method of Supply-demand Balancing Capability considering VPP deployment
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Recently, Virtual Power Plant (VPP) has attracted attention for supply-demand balancing capability, but the control methodology for VPP realization is still at a study phase. In this study, VPP is assumed to have many aggregators whereas each aggregator integrates numerous battery resources, and manages a local energy grid like Microgrid. This study presents an allocation method of supply-demand balancing capability by an aggregator considering state of charge (SOC) of battery.

articleTitle: Research on the Control Method based on Virtual Synchronous Machine Technology of AC/DC Distribution Device
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper proposes a control method based on virtual synchronous machine technology of AC/DC distribution device, including DC voltage loop, power loop, AC voltage loop and current loop. The control method helps multiple sources and AC/DC loads integration. The AC/DC distribution device can emulate the characteristics of synchronous generator, including primary frequency modulation, primary voltage modulation, inertia and excitation characteristics. To improve the dynamic performance, the AC voltage and current dual-loop is cascaded after the power loop. In the whole process of operation, the energy is exchanged through DC bus and the DC bus voltage is stable. The simulation validates the proposed control strategies.

articleTitle: Multi-Hop Network Based Coordination of Converters in DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Microgrids with power electronic converters at major interfaces between sources and sinks of energy, such as DC microgrids, present an opportunity for highly specific routing of energy if converters are coordinated appropriately. Developments in SiC power devices are yielding converters with far greater switching frequencies than Si based devices resulting in an order of magnitude reduction of the control time scales as compared to converter systems utilizing conventional IGBTs. In addition there has been continued development toward more modular converter systems. Both of those trends have resulted in the use of FPGA-based control platforms for power electronic systems. Increasing communication and computational capabilities of new FPGA based controllers provides opportunities beyond simply supporting high speed converters. Fast control coordination across the system using a multi-hop communication architecture provides a degree of energy management not previously realizable in microgrids.

articleTitle: Fuel cell and Electrolyzer System for Supply and Demand Balancing in DC
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: DC-feeding Microgrid (DCMG) which can integrate plural DC-driven facilities by using information is considered as a future energy system for rural shore area. To balance supply and demand in the DCMG, a set of fuel cells and electrolyzer (FCE) systems is proposed as an energy storage system instead of conventional battery systems. DCMG including FCE, PV and DC loads are assumed, the mode controlling method for FCE to balance supply and demand is proposed in this paper. As a result, FCE is controlled by proposed method and can balance supply and demand without reverse power flow to utility grid.

articleTitle: Power Flow Calculation of Shipboard DC Microgrid Power System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In recent years, the regulations of emission from governments are becoming increasingly stricter, the fuel-efficiency requirement from energy users are also rising correspondingly. It results in the current trends towards more efficient ships, the most representative concept is the All-Electric-Ship (AES), which exploits the electrical propulsion system instead of conventional mechanical propulsion system. One of the current research trends of shipboard power system is focused on DC power distribution system, especially the system analysis of shipboard DC microgrid, in which the power flow calculation is a very important and essential topic. Power flow calculation is the fundamental part of power system design and analysis. The purpose is to provide a quantitative description of voltage and power distribution in the system, under given system parameters and operating modes. In this paper, power flow calculation of a typical shipboard DC microgrid is presented, including the voltage of each node, the current of each branch, and the main loop state of each major equipment. Results of the calculation will provide the essential basis data for a series of follow-up tasks. Power flow calculation is the fundamental part of power system design and analysis. The purpose is to provide a quantitative description of voltage and power distribution in the system, under given system parameters and operating modes. In this paper, power flow calculation of a typical shipboard DC microgrid is presented, including the voltage of each node, the current of each branch, and the main loop state of each major equipment. Results of the calculation will provide the essential basis data for a series of follow-up tasks.

articleTitle: Terminal Capacitor Compensation Based Stability Design for DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper investigates the detailed elements of a DC microgrid that might cause instability, and proposes a stabilizing guidance based on the passive stability criterion. For illustration purpose, the terminal output impedance model of a source side power converter under double loop with droop control is built, and its frequency characteristics are analyzed. It is found that the instant high power absorption from the microgrid might make the source side power converter's output to oscillate. The details of how the circuit and control elements in the source side impact the terminal impedance are illustrated. This paper shows that the stability of plug and play performance of DC microgrid can be guaranteed with the proposed stabilization methods. A Matlab/Simulink model is used to validate the analysis.

articleTitle: Study of a microgrid using a private power generator during a utility grid failure
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This study investigates the dynamic characteristics of a microgrid using a private power generator during a utility grid failure. If a utility grid failure occurs, the frequency and voltage of the generator will fluctuate. However, load power must always be of high quality. Therefore, continuing operation while suppressing the fluctuation of the voltage and frequency of the power generator is necessary. The generator is connected to the input or output side of the uninterruptible power system (UPS) of the microgrid, and the dynamic characteristics when the utility grid failure occurs are examined. By connecting the generator to the output side of the UPS, supplying power to the load without it being affected by the utility grid failure is possible.

articleTitle: Experimental study on interruption time in two inductance for 100 V class DC breaking arc
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In this paper, DC breaking experiments were carried out in the range of 10 to 100 A by using simple arc-quenching device. The influence of the circuit inductance on arc breaking time are discussed. DC arc quenching device is connected to DC power source of 100 V through resistance R, inductance L and switch S. In the experiments, the anode separates from the cathode at a time of t=0 ms and subsequently moves upward with an average velocity of around 1.2 m/s by electromagnetic coil. The maximum distance between electrodes is 30 mm which is reached at t=28 ms. Inductors of 0, 1.2 and 3 mH are inserted into a circuit. The major achievement in this study are as follows. (a) The arcing time is longer in the case of L=3 mH than that of L=0 mH. (b) The DC current-limiting interruption might be successfully accomplished by realizing the arc voltage which is higher than the power supply voltage. (c) Even if the arc column was lengthened by the Lorenz force, it is found by estimating the actual arc length that arc column per unit length has the unique transient behavior.

articleTitle: Finite-State Predictive Power Control based Interlink Converter for AC-DC Micro-grid
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper present the finite-state predictive power control (FS-PPC) for the interlinking converter in the micro-grid. The proportional-integral (PI) based controllers are dynamically slower for the sudden changes in the power reference values. The phase lock loop (PLL) is essential requirement for such algorithms. The FS-PPC has faster dynamic response as compare to PI based controller in tracking the reference values. The FS-PPC is proposed to control the power flow between the DC and AC micro-grids. The developed control provides the constant switching frequency operation for the interlinking converter which reduces the ripples and total harmonic distortion of the grid current in order to follow the grid codes. Simulation results are provided for the validity of the control algorithm.

articleTitle: An Experimental Analysis of Frequency Characteristics in LLC Resonant Converter with Cockcroft-Walton Circuit
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: High step-up DC-DC converters with the Cockcroft-Walton (CW) circuit are used for high DC voltage power supplies such as an electron beam irradiation device, a particle accelerator, and an insulation test device. As these devices are large and heavy, reducing the size is required. High frequency operation generally reduces the value of passive devices: an inductor and a capacitor. However, the switching loss increases at high frequency operation. Therefore, an LLC resonant converter has attracted attention because it maintains Zero Voltage Switching (ZVS) for high efficiency. This report proposes an LLC resonant converter with the CW circuit as the rectifier. In addition, the additional inductor in the CW circuit occurs the LC resonance for increasing the output voltage. As a result, the proposed DC-DC converter achieves both ZVS and high step-up. This report experimentally clarifies the verification of the proposed DC-DC converter.

articleTitle: Voltage Dip Mitigation Techniques for Medium-Voltage DC Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper presents a very efficient topology for transient voltage dip mitigation for high power MVDC grids. A dedicated boost converter is combined with a threephase rectifier to form a DC grid, with the advantages of being reliable, applicable for high power applications and dip immune without using energy storage. To describe the operational behavior of power transfer capability, a mathematical model is derived and compared with numerical simulation.

articleTitle: An Experimental Study on Extinguishing Property of DC Arc Ignited with Disconnection of Activated PV Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The introduction of photovoltaic power generation systems (PV-systems) is being encouraged and advanced as a matter of national policy in Japan. When the arc discharge occurs on the DC side by disconnection or short-circuit fault, it should be extinguished as soon as possible in order to prevent an expansion to a fire faults. In this report, as a first step, we focused on DC arc caused by disconnection of solar cell array and experimentally investigated the process of its occurrence and disappearance.

articleTitle: Method of Determining Operation Voltage of Dispersed Photovoltaic Generator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In this study, we propose a method to calculate the optimum operating voltage for establishing spatial fairness in photovoltaic power generation (PV) using only the information of its own node. With the introduction of a large amount of PV, there is concern that unfairness in power generation output and installation capacity will occur among customers in the current control system. Spatial equity can be cited as one of the items to notice. To establish the effectiveness of the method proposed in this study, we examine three cases. We found that the operation voltage can be determined independently by using the low-pressure system alone. In addition, as a result of actually examining the operating voltage, we were able to secure spatial fairness.

articleTitle: 350 kVA Multi-Function Converters for DC-Microgrid Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In a dc-microgrid, ac is harmonized with dc, and therefore, a multi-function converter is required to transfer power between ac and dc grids. This paper presents design and implementation of converters with multiple functions that include grid-connection (GC) mode, uninterruptible power supply (UPS) mode, and mode transition. Control laws for the GC and UPS modes based on a direct digital control with division-summation (D- Σ) processes are presented in detail. During operation, mode transition between the two modes is discussed. Experimental and simulated results from two 350 kVA multi-function converters with circulating power test are used to verify the analyses, designs and discussions.

articleTitle: A Verification on a Zero-Current Detection Method of Interleaved Boost Chopper with High Frequency Operation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This study aims to reduce the size of a chopper applied to photovoltaic strings. For high frequency switching operation with SiC-MOSFETs, an interleaved topology is applied to the converter to reduce switching losses and inductor and capacitor sizes. High speed zero-current detection is essential for achieving soft switching during turn-on period. Here, a zero-current detection circuit is proposed, and experimental results show high efficiency converter operation using the detection circuit.

articleTitle: Hybrid magnetic EMI filter design for Low Voltage DC distribution (LVDC) network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The integrated EMI filter approach is an effective solution to miniaturize the overall EMI filter dimensions especially in LVDC. The hybrid magnetic approach offers synergistic effects by merging benefits of different magnetic materials to attenuate conducted emission efficiently.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of GaN-MPPT by Transient Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In this paper, the performance of maximum power point tracking (MPPT) using gallium nitride and silicon semiconductors were evaluated based on the difference in their transient characteristics. A solar power generation system increases its power generation efficiency by controlling the MPPT. Due to higher efficiency and smaller device size, gallium nitride and silicon carbide semiconductors have attracted more attention as next-generation power semiconductors than Si semiconductors. This study confirms that the power conversion efficiency of MPPT devices can be improved by using GaN semiconductors.

articleTitle: Arc-Free Bidirectional Hybrid DC Switch using Tungsten or Tungsten-clad Copper Contacts
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: A hybrid DC switch has been studied intensively because of the increasing demand for photovoltaic power stations and DC power distribution systems. The hybrid DC switch, consisting of mechanical contacts, semiconductor devices, and metal-oxide varistors, has the advantages of low contact resistance, high-speed current interruption, and a short-duration arc during current commutation. Moreover, arc-free current interruption is possible if the boiling voltage of the contact material exceeds the circuit voltage needed for turning on the semiconductor devices. A combination of tungsten contacts and SiC-MOSFETs satisfies this condition. As a result, an arc-free current interruption of 220 A was achieved with two-pole-tungsten contacts for bidirectional DC switching, where two SiC-MOSFETs were connected in series. The newly developed tungsten-clad copper contacts increased the threshold current of arc-free commutation up to 260 A.

articleTitle: An Inverter Control Method for Remote Island Electric Power System Constituted by Renewable Energy Sources
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In this paper, the author assumes that electric power in a remote island is supplied only by renewable energies and energy storages. Specifically, the combination of photovoltaic power generation and storage battery is assumed basics and the constitution of power supply system connecting with inverter is shown. A control method of the inverter is suggested and inspection examples by the simulation are shown.

articleTitle: Influence of voltage rise suppression control with constant output power at the introduction of large photovoltaic device to the end of distribution system
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In recent years, an introduction of the photovoltaic (PV) devices has been increasing by promoting the use of renewable energy. The magnitude of the receiving-end voltage is influenced by the PV output power and the impedance of the distribution line. In this paper, we focused leading power factor controls of the power conditioning system for suppression of the receiving end voltage rise. The influences of the controls on PV output power, line loss and power inflowing to substation were qualitatively analyzed by using vector diagrams. The leading power factor required to suppress the voltage rise to the specified value was quantitatively discussed.

articleTitle: Storage Battery Capacity Reduction Effect on 400V-class DC Power Supplied Office with Consideration for Renewable Energy Ratio
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In this paper, we derive the relationship between the storage battery capacity reduction effect and the renewable energy ratio (RER) in a building by numerically analyzing each demand curve according to the building use when applying a 400 V-class DC power distribution system. Furthermore, from the numerical analysis results, we report the evaluation results of the condition where the DC power distribution system is more advantageous than the AC power distribution system.

articleTitle: Study on the Surveying Wiring Path in Solar Power Generation System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This study proposes a novel cable detection method to survey the electrical wiring in buildings and factories comprising several types of equipment with numerous cable connections. The wiring is implemented usually in conduits concealed inside the walls and beneath the floors to a massive extent with the cables of different types laid for hundreds of meters. Prior to the removal of a defective cable in repair work, it is necessary to identify it correctly. A cable locator is used for the identification of a cable in a complex wiring system without damaging the healthy cables erroneously so that a circuit breaker would not trip due to a cable fault eventually. Cable locators are commercially available in the market and the detection method is classified into two types: electromagnetic induction and electrostatic induction. In this study, a new cable locator is developed and demonstrated, and different types of cable locator are evaluated.

articleTitle: Distributed High Step-Down Ratio DC Transformer for Interconnection of MVDC and LVDC Grids
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: DC grid technology is regarded as a promising solution for future electric networks integrating a great amount of DC renewable energies, DC loads. For the fault ride-through requirements in the DC grid, this article proposes a new distributed high step-down ratio DC transformer, which consists of two parts. The front stage implements the capabilities of buck and fault ride-through. The latter stage implements the functions of voltage controlling and isolation. Related simulations verify the validity and feasibility.

articleTitle: Voltage-Frequency Control in PV Introduction System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: We developed a new power flow calculation method considering frequency. Because frequency calculation is not included in the normal power flow calculation, and therefore, in the power system in which solar power system is introduced, the frequency characteristic is not taken into consideration at all in the rise of the voltage when surplus electric power is generated. In this study, we propose a control method for voltage and frequency using a new power flow calculation.

articleTitle: Verification of arc discharge phenomenon and connection reliability
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: It is known that the arc discharge phenomenon occurs when the DC power supply is cut off. The arc discharge phenomenon has been verified for many of the literature etc. that exceeds 400 V dc / 10 A class voltage currents, but in our research it can lead to a big accident in micro arc regardless of voltage know. In this paper, we identify the cause of the accident caused by the arc discharge phenomenon generated by the low voltage direct current and show the countermeasure.

articleTitle: Development of Sodium Sulfur Battery
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: NGK has developed a sodium sulfur battery (NAS battery) for load leveling applications, allowing the grid to deal with increasing peak. The recent growth in environmentally friendly renewable energies causes network instability. A secondary battery based energy storage system is seen as one of the strongest solutions to stabilize the network while improving the efficiency and usability of these renewable energy technologies. The NAS battery features long duration discharge, compactness, and a long lifespan of 15 years. The capacity for long duration discharge is one of the most notable features of this technology, a feature which becomes more important as renewable energy generation increases.

articleTitle: Verification of dc Capacitor Control of Modular Multilevel Converters for dc Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Modular multilevel converters (MMC) have been studied for ac-dc conversion in high-voltage direct-current (HVDC) grids. The dc capacitor voltage of each cell must be in balance so that MMCs can maintain the dc bus voltage. This paper presents schemes for interphase balancing control and upper and lower arm balance control using the negative sequence components of the current output to the ac grid and the circulating current.

articleTitle: Power Module for Low Voltage DC Hybrid Circuit Breaker
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper presents design and development of a power module used in a low voltage DC hybrid circuit breaker (HCB). The novel power module is rated for 125 A / 380 V and can interrupt electrical faults within approximately 300 μs in a power grid with up to 20 kA short-circuit capacity. The designed module employs an auxiliary power electronics switch including 30 V silicon MOSFETs with very low on-state resistance in series with an innovative high-speed and low ohmic mechanical switch. This enables completely arc-free switching. A main power electronics switch consisting of bare-die 1.2 kV IGBTs and SiC Merged PIN Schottky diodes is used for current interruption. These components characterized in previous publications are attached on an Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> substrate in such a way that the smallest possible inductive loss from current commutation loop and a reduced footprint are obtained. Additionally, a galvanic separation relay and integrated current measurement shunts are included. Finally, the substrate is placed on a Cu baseplate and encapsulated in both soft and hard encapsulations similar to standard power IGBT modules. Experimental results on fault current commutation and interruption, minimum required air gap for the mechanical switch, and steady state thermal characteristics are reported here. The findings enable the realization of the most compact and reliable HCB with the highest available power density currently feasible.

articleTitle: Fault Identification and Interruption Methods in Low Voltage DC Grids — A Review
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: An increasing number of electrical loads and sources in the distribution grid require a conversion step from DC, or AC at variable frequency, to be connected to the traditional 50/60Hz AC grid. This sparks an increasing interest for Low Voltage DC microgrids as an alternative. LVDC grids enable a reduction of the losses and an increase of the transfer capacity compared to their AC equivalent. However, fast and selective fault protection still remains a major obstacle for the breakthrough of LVDC grids. The challenge is twofold: On the one hand, a protection strategy for fast fault identification is required, on the other hand there is a need for protection devices capable of fast fault clearance in an LVDC grid. This paper first gives an overview of the current state-of-the-art of fault indicators and methods for fault identification in DC grids, addressing the first part of the challenge. Subsequently, an overview is given of the interruption devices that are currently available for fault clearance in DC grids and their (dis)advantages, addressing the second challenge.

articleTitle: Weakly Meshing the Radial Distribution Networks with Power Electronic Based Flexible DC Interlinks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Flexible dc interlinks can be used for compact and efficient active power redirection by creating a meshed structure in existing radial distribution network. It is shown that with optimal location and sizing of a back-to-back voltage sourced converter based point-to-point dc link connecting two ac buses of the test 33-bus radial distribution system, 10-15% network loss minimization can be achieved. This possibility can be advantageous in efficiently redirecting active power flows in urban and semi -urban areas because intermittent distributed grid resources (such as photovoltaics and wind farms) and energy intensive loads (such as ultra fast charging stations for electric vehicles) are resulting in local pockets of excess generation and demand. The impact of distributed generation and high powered loads on placement of dc interlink is numerically quantified to suggest that both capacity and efficiency enhancement can be achieved in the distribution grid. It is envisioned that this method of integrating dc power transmission can be the first realistic step towards realizing a multi-terminal dc medium voltage distribution evolving out of the existing infrastructure.

articleTitle: Integrated Charging of EVs Using Existing LVDC Light Rail Infrastructure: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE Third International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
